newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits little changed ahead of CPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were little changed in moderate trade, dealers said on Tuesday.
Most traders were sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. May consumer price index (CPI), housing starts and industrial production and capacity utilisation data.
The consumer price index for May is forecast to show an increase of 0.2 percent compared with a 0.1 percent gain reported in April.
May housing starts is expected to be around 1.47 million annnualised units against April's 1.473 million units.
Industrial production for May is expected to show a gain of 0.2 percent from a 0.6 percent increase in April while May capacity utilisation is expected to be unchanged from April's 83.4 percent.

"The market was quiet and featureless in the morning except for some light activity at the short end of the market. Some people are waiting for market direction from tonight's release of the consumer price index, housing starts, industrial production and capacity utilisation figures," a dealer said.
"But I don't think there will be much impact unless the numbers are way off market expectations," he said.
In day-to-day rates, Tuesday/Wednesday and Wednesday/Thursday were unchanged from Monday's common 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, respectively. Week-fixed eased 1/16 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months eased 1/16 point to 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, four-months was unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8, six-months unchanged at 5-7/8 5-3/4 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-1/16 5-15/16 percent.
